lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, everyone's here. This is the Nanyang Kopi and Toast launch check for Raffles Place. Four items today: the kiosk Kopi names, the morning seat crunch, cash at the kiosks, then the MakanWithZack butter video.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Mei, let's start with the kiosk. What did the trial show?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yesterday's trial had 28 first-time users. Nineteen of them froze for over two minutes at Kopi O Kosong, Kopi C Siew Dai or Teh Halia.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Seventy-two percent never noticed the small language toggle in the corner.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Renaming the buttons is not free. The kitchen docket prints the same name the customer sees, so the uncles would have to read the English name.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: When we tested that at Tampines, drink prep slowed by fifteen seconds a cup. And the fifteen-inch screen only fits twelve buttons per page.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: So what helps a first-timer without slowing the kitchen?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: I can try a clearer drink step, but I don't know if it fits the twelve-button grid.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I can check what fits tonight, but any label change needs a kitchen test before eight.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Mei, can you file a ticket for the kiosk label experiment so it is tracked with the trial numbers?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Yes, I'll file it today with the nineteen out of twenty-eight numbers.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Do we know if tourists or locals struggled more?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: The trial sheet has that split, but I haven't looked at it since last week.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, that is the kiosk item. Let's move to the morning seat crunch.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Our twenty-eight seats were jammed again this morning.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Four laptop freelancers held our four 4-seater booths, that's sixteen seats, for two hours on a single two-dollar-twenty Kopi O.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: That is about four hundred and twenty dollars in lost breakfast sets. And Auntie Mary is still shaken after that guy in a suit yelled at her.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Sixty percent of our morning customers dine solo. They cannot carry a hot tray of runny eggs without a table.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The twelve booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi run on a smart relay breaker in the back room. I can cut power, but that also hits paying customers.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Who enforces any new seating rule if it cannot be Auntie Mary?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: That is the hard part. If we ban tissue packets, a solo diner with a hot tray has nowhere to sit while the queue clears.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I still have the numbered table pucks in the storeroom, but I don't know if handing them out after payment fixes the queue.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: How many solo diners actually need a table between eight and ten? Do we have that number?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Not per hour. The trial sheet has the split, but I would have to check it.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, let's not decide blind. Put the per-hour solo diner number on the list.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I can pull the socket usage from the relay, but that won't tell us who is a camper.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Fine, keep that open. Moving on to cash at the kiosks.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, you raised the cash clip.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: A seventy-four-year-old regular was turned away at the NO CASH sign and the TikTok clip is at forty thousand views.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Fourteen retired regulars walked out. Ninety-four percent of them carry only two- and ten-dollar notes, so a two-dollar-twenty Kopi needs change.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: The kiosks cannot take cash tomorrow. A physical bill-acceptor costs fourteen hundred dollars and takes three weeks.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And the toast counter cannot take cash. Money handling and ready-to-eat food must stay separate, so staff who touch coins change gloves and wash hands, plus forty seconds an order.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Counting the float at night already costs three hundred and eighty a month in overtime, and both toast staff are flat out at eight.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So who runs cash, and how do we make it visible enough that TikTok stops calling us anti-elderly?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: I don't have a spare till or cashier terminal at the front either.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And how is change counted and balanced at close?

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: That is still open. Nothing we have can take cash tomorrow without a free pair of hands.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Okay, cash is not settled. Last item, the butter video.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, where are we with Zack?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: MakanWithZack posted a reel saying our kaya butter toast has half as much cold butter as Ya Kun. It has ninety thousand views.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: He will film an eight-thirty live re-taste tomorrow for six hundred cash, or four-fifty plus twenty plushies from our storeroom.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: Our twelve-gram slab did not shrink. It stays thick on a dine-in plate but melts flat in a closed takeaway box with hot toast.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: A separate chilled cup costs five cents a box, and a vented box is available too. I would need to test them at the counter.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Anchor butter is up thirty-five percent. Doubling to twenty grams adds forty-two cents a set, about eleven hundred a month in margin, and we only have seven hundred and fifty left in the launch budget.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: Regular customers queue right behind Zack, so an influencer-only portion or a secret button will be seen.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What do we show on camera, and how do we prove regulars get the same portion?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: I can show the twelve-gram slab and the takeaway box, but we still have to choose what changes permanently.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Daniel, can you email Zack and confirm the eight-thirty re-taste for tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes, I'll email Zack tonight and confirm the details.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: And I'll post the final plan in the team channel once we settle the butter decision.

lines.speaker: Arjun
lines.text: We still haven't settled the portion, though.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Right, keep the portion open for now. That's everything.

lines.speaker: Wei Ling
lines.text: Thanks all, good meeting.
